scenes.setting: Athens. A room in the Palace of Theseus

lines.text: Enter Theseus, Hippolyta, Philostrate and Attendants.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Now, fair Hippolyta, our nuptial hour

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Draws on apace; four happy days bring in

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Another moon; but oh, methinks, how slow

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: This old moon wanes! She lingers my desires,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Like to a step-dame or a dowager,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Long withering out a young man’s revenue.

lines.speaker: HIPPOLYTA
lines.text: Four days will quickly steep themselves in night;

lines.speaker: HIPPOLYTA
lines.text: Four nights will quickly dream away the time;

lines.speaker: HIPPOLYTA
lines.text: And then the moon, like to a silver bow

lines.speaker: HIPPOLYTA
lines.text: New bent in heaven, shall behold the night

lines.speaker: HIPPOLYTA
lines.text: Of our solemnities.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Go, Philostrate,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Stir up the Athenian youth to merriments;

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Awake the pert and nimble spirit of mirth;

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Turn melancholy forth to funerals;

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: The pale companion is not for our pomp.
[_Exit Philostrate._]

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Hippolyta, I woo’d thee with my sword,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: And won thy love doing thee injuries;

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: But I will wed thee in another key,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: With pomp, with triumph, and with revelling.
Enter Egeus, Hermia, Lysander and Demetrius.

lines.speaker: EGEUS
lines.text: Happy be Theseus, our renownèd Duke!

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Thanks, good Egeus. What’s the news with thee?

lines.speaker: EGEUS
lines.text: Full of vexation come I, with complaint

lines.speaker: EGEUS
lines.text: Against my child, my daughter Hermia.

lines.speaker: EGEUS
lines.text: Stand forth, Demetrius. My noble lord,

lines.speaker: EGEUS
lines.text: This man hath my consent to marry her.

lines.speaker: EGEUS
lines.text: Stand forth, Lysander. And, my gracious Duke,

lines.speaker: EGEUS
lines.text: This man hath bewitch’d the bosom of my child.

lines.speaker: EGEUS
lines.text: Thou, thou, Lysander, thou hast given her rhymes,

lines.speaker: EGEUS
lines.text: And interchang’d love-tokens with my child.

lines.speaker: EGEUS
lines.text: Thou hast by moonlight at her window sung,

lines.speaker: EGEUS
lines.text: With feigning voice, verses of feigning love;

lines.speaker: EGEUS
lines.text: And stol’n the impression of her fantasy

lines.speaker: EGEUS
lines.text: With bracelets of thy hair, rings, gauds, conceits,

lines.speaker: EGEUS
lines.text: Knacks, trifles, nosegays, sweetmeats (messengers

lines.speaker: EGEUS
lines.text: Of strong prevailment in unharden’d youth)

lines.speaker: EGEUS
lines.text: With cunning hast thou filch’d my daughter’s heart,

lines.speaker: EGEUS
lines.text: Turn’d her obedience (which is due to me)

lines.speaker: EGEUS
lines.text: To stubborn harshness. And, my gracious Duke,

lines.speaker: EGEUS
lines.text: Be it so she will not here before your grace

lines.speaker: EGEUS
lines.text: Consent to marry with Demetrius,

lines.speaker: EGEUS
lines.text: I beg the ancient privilege of Athens:

lines.speaker: EGEUS
lines.text: As she is mine I may dispose of her;

lines.speaker: EGEUS
lines.text: Which shall be either to this gentleman

lines.speaker: EGEUS
lines.text: Or to her death, according to our law

lines.speaker: EGEUS
lines.text: Immediately provided in that case.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: What say you, Hermia? Be advis’d, fair maid.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: To you your father should be as a god;

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: One that compos’d your beauties, yea, and one

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: To whom you are but as a form in wax

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: By him imprinted, and within his power

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: To leave the figure, or disfigure it.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Demetrius is a worthy gentleman.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: So is Lysander.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: In himself he is.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: But in this kind, wanting your father’s voice,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: The other must be held the worthier.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: I would my father look’d but with my eyes.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Rather your eyes must with his judgment look.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: I do entreat your Grace to pardon me.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: I know not by what power I am made bold,

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Nor how it may concern my modesty

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: In such a presence here to plead my thoughts:

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: But I beseech your Grace that I may know

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: The worst that may befall me in this case,

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: If I refuse to wed Demetrius.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Either to die the death, or to abjure

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: For ever the society of men.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Therefore, fair Hermia, question your desires,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Know of your youth, examine well your blood,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Whether, if you yield not to your father’s choice,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: You can endure the livery of a nun,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: For aye to be in shady cloister mew’d,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: To live a barren sister all your life,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Chanting faint hymns to the cold fruitless moon.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Thrice-blessèd they that master so their blood

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: To undergo such maiden pilgrimage,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: But earthlier happy is the rose distill’d

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Than that which, withering on the virgin thorn,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Grows, lives, and dies, in single blessedness.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: So will I grow, so live, so die, my lord,

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Ere I will yield my virgin patent up

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Unto his lordship, whose unwishèd yoke

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: My soul consents not to give sovereignty.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Take time to pause; and by the next new moon

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: The sealing-day betwixt my love and me

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: For everlasting bond of fellowship,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Upon that day either prepare to die

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: For disobedience to your father’s will,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Or else to wed Demetrius, as he would,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Or on Diana’s altar to protest

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: For aye austerity and single life.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Relent, sweet Hermia; and, Lysander, yield

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Thy crazèd title to my certain right.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: You have her father’s love, Demetrius.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Let me have Hermia’s. Do you marry him.

lines.speaker: EGEUS
lines.text: Scornful Lysander, true, he hath my love;

lines.speaker: EGEUS
lines.text: And what is mine my love shall render him;

lines.speaker: EGEUS
lines.text: And she is mine, and all my right of her

lines.speaker: EGEUS
lines.text: I do estate unto Demetrius.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: I am, my lord, as well deriv’d as he,

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: As well possess’d; my love is more than his;

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: My fortunes every way as fairly rank’d,

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: If not with vantage, as Demetrius’;

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: And, which is more than all these boasts can be,

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: I am belov’d of beauteous Hermia.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Why should not I then prosecute my right?

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Demetrius, I’ll avouch it to his head,

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Made love to Nedar’s daughter, Helena,

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: And won her soul; and she, sweet lady, dotes,

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Devoutly dotes, dotes in idolatry,

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Upon this spotted and inconstant man.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: I must confess that I have heard so much,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: And with Demetrius thought to have spoke thereof;

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: But, being over-full of self-affairs,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: My mind did lose it.—But, Demetrius, come,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: And come, Egeus; you shall go with me.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: I have some private schooling for you both.—

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: For you, fair Hermia, look you arm yourself

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: To fit your fancies to your father’s will,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Or else the law of Athens yields you up

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: (Which by no means we may extenuate)

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: To death, or to a vow of single life.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Come, my Hippolyta. What cheer, my love?

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Demetrius and Egeus, go along;

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: I must employ you in some business

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Against our nuptial, and confer with you

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Of something nearly that concerns yourselves.

lines.speaker: EGEUS
lines.text: With duty and desire we follow you.
[_Exeunt all but Lysander and Hermia._]

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: How now, my love? Why is your cheek so pale?

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: How chance the roses there do fade so fast?

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Belike for want of rain, which I could well

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Beteem them from the tempest of my eyes.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Ay me! For aught that I could ever read,

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Could ever hear by tale or history,

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: The course of true love never did run smooth.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: But either it was different in blood—

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: O cross! Too high to be enthrall’d to low.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Or else misgraffèd in respect of years—

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: O spite! Too old to be engag’d to young.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Or else it stood upon the choice of friends—

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: O hell! to choose love by another’s eyes!

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Or, if there were a sympathy in choice,

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: War, death, or sickness did lay siege to it,

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Making it momentany as a sound,

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Swift as a shadow, short as any dream,

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Brief as the lightning in the collied night

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: That, in a spleen, unfolds both heaven and earth,

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: And, ere a man hath power to say, ‘Behold!’

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: The jaws of darkness do devour it up:

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: So quick bright things come to confusion.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: If then true lovers have ever cross’d,

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: It stands as an edict in destiny.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Then let us teach our trial patience,

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Because it is a customary cross,

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: As due to love as thoughts and dreams and sighs,

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Wishes and tears, poor fancy’s followers.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: A good persuasion; therefore, hear me, Hermia.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: I have a widow aunt, a dowager

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Of great revenue, and she hath no child.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: From Athens is her house remote seven leagues,

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: And she respects me as her only son.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: There, gentle Hermia, may I marry thee,

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: And to that place the sharp Athenian law

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Cannot pursue us. If thou lovest me then,

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Steal forth thy father’s house tomorrow night;

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: And in the wood, a league without the town

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: (Where I did meet thee once with Helena

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: To do observance to a morn of May),

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: There will I stay for thee.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: My good Lysander!

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: I swear to thee by Cupid’s strongest bow,

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: By his best arrow with the golden head,

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: By the simplicity of Venus’ doves,

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: By that which knitteth souls and prospers loves,

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: And by that fire which burn’d the Carthage queen

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: When the false Trojan under sail was seen,

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: By all the vows that ever men have broke

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: (In number more than ever women spoke),

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: In that same place thou hast appointed me,

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Tomorrow truly will I meet with thee.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Keep promise, love. Look, here comes Helena.
Enter Helena.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: God speed fair Helena! Whither away?

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Call you me fair? That fair again unsay.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Demetrius loves your fair. O happy fair!

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Your eyes are lode-stars and your tongue’s sweet air

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: More tuneable than lark to shepherd’s ear,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: When wheat is green, when hawthorn buds appear.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Sickness is catching. O were favour so,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Yours would I catch, fair Hermia, ere I go.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: My ear should catch your voice, my eye your eye,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: My tongue should catch your tongue’s sweet melody.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Were the world mine, Demetrius being bated,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: The rest I’d give to be to you translated.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: O, teach me how you look, and with what art

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: You sway the motion of Demetrius’ heart!

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: I frown upon him, yet he loves me still.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: O that your frowns would teach my smiles such skill!

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: I give him curses, yet he gives me love.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: O that my prayers could such affection move!

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: The more I hate, the more he follows me.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: The more I love, the more he hateth me.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: His folly, Helena, is no fault of mine.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: None but your beauty; would that fault were mine!

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Take comfort: he no more shall see my face;

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Lysander and myself will fly this place.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Before the time I did Lysander see,

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Seem’d Athens as a paradise to me.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: O, then, what graces in my love do dwell,

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: That he hath turn’d a heaven into hell!

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Helen, to you our minds we will unfold:

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Tomorrow night, when Phoebe doth behold

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Her silver visage in the watery glass,

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Decking with liquid pearl the bladed grass

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: (A time that lovers’ flights doth still conceal),

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Through Athens’ gates have we devis’d to steal.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: And in the wood where often you and I

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Upon faint primrose beds were wont to lie,

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Emptying our bosoms of their counsel sweet,

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: There my Lysander and myself shall meet,

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: And thence from Athens turn away our eyes,

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: To seek new friends and stranger companies.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Farewell, sweet playfellow. Pray thou for us,

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: And good luck grant thee thy Demetrius!

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Keep word, Lysander. We must starve our sight

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: From lovers’ food, till morrow deep midnight.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: I will, my Hermia.
[_Exit Hermia._]

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Helena, adieu.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: As you on him, Demetrius dote on you!
[_Exit Lysander._]

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: How happy some o’er other some can be!

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Through Athens I am thought as fair as she.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: But what of that? Demetrius thinks not so;

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: He will not know what all but he do know.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: And as he errs, doting on Hermia’s eyes,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: So I, admiring of his qualities.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Things base and vile, holding no quantity,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Love can transpose to form and dignity.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Love looks not with the eyes, but with the mind;

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: And therefore is wing’d Cupid painted blind.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Nor hath love’s mind of any judgment taste.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Wings, and no eyes, figure unheedy haste.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: And therefore is love said to be a child,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Because in choice he is so oft beguil’d.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: As waggish boys in game themselves forswear,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: So the boy Love is perjur’d everywhere.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: For, ere Demetrius look’d on Hermia’s eyne,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: He hail’d down oaths that he was only mine;

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: And when this hail some heat from Hermia felt,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: So he dissolv’d, and showers of oaths did melt.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: I will go tell him of fair Hermia’s flight.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Then to the wood will he tomorrow night

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Pursue her; and for this intelligence

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: If I have thanks, it is a dear expense.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: But herein mean I to enrich my pain,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: To have his sight thither and back again.
[_Exit Helena._]

scenes.setting: The Same. A Room in a Cottage

lines.text: Enter Quince, Snug, Bottom, Flute, Snout  and Starveling.

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: Is all our company here?

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: You were best to call them generally, man by man, according to the

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: scrip.

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: Here is the scroll of every man’s name, which is thought fit through

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: all Athens, to play in our interlude before the Duke and Duchess, on

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: his wedding-day at night.

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: First, good Peter Quince, say what the play treats on; then read the

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: names of the actors; and so grow to a point.

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: Marry, our play is _The most lamentable comedy and most cruel death of

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: Pyramus and Thisbe_.

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: A very good piece of work, I assure you, and a merry. Now, good Peter

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: Quince, call forth your actors by the scroll. Masters, spread

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: yourselves.

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: Answer, as I call you. Nick Bottom, the weaver.

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: Ready. Name what part I am for, and proceed.

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: You, Nick Bottom, are set down for Pyramus.

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: What is Pyramus—a lover, or a tyrant?

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: A lover, that kills himself most gallantly for love.

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: That will ask some tears in the true performing of it. If I do it, let

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: the audience look to their eyes. I will move storms; I will condole in

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: some measure. To the rest—yet my chief humour is for a tyrant. I could

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: play Ercles rarely, or a part to tear a cat in, to make all split.

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: The raging rocks

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: And shivering shocks

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: Shall break the locks

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: Of prison gates,

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: And Phibbus’ car

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: Shall shine from far,

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: And make and mar

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: The foolish Fates.

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: This was lofty. Now name the rest of the players. This is Ercles’ vein,

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: a tyrant’s vein; a lover is more condoling.

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: Francis Flute, the bellows-mender.

lines.speaker: FLUTE
lines.text: Here, Peter Quince.

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: Flute, you must take Thisbe on you.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: But I shall do thee mischief in the wood.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Ay, in the temple, in the town, the field,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: You do me mischief. Fie, Demetrius!

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Your wrongs do set a scandal on my sex.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: We cannot fight for love as men may do.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: We should be woo’d, and were not made to woo.
[_Exit Demetrius._]

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: I’ll follow thee, and make a heaven of hell,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: To die upon the hand I love so well.
[_Exit Helena._]

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Fare thee well, nymph. Ere he do leave this grove,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Thou shalt fly him, and he shall seek thy love.
Enter Puck.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Hast thou the flower there? Welcome, wanderer.

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Ay, there it is.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: I pray thee give it me.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: I know a bank where the wild thyme blows,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Where oxlips and the nodding violet grows,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Quite over-canopied with luscious woodbine,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: With sweet musk-roses, and with eglantine.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: There sleeps Titania sometime of the night,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Lull’d in these flowers with dances and delight;

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: And there the snake throws her enamell’d skin,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Weed wide enough to wrap a fairy in.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: And with the juice of this I’ll streak her eyes,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: And make her full of hateful fantasies.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Take thou some of it, and seek through this grove:

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: A sweet Athenian lady is in love

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: With a disdainful youth. Anoint his eyes;

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: But do it when the next thing he espies

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: May be the lady. Thou shalt know the man

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: By the Athenian garments he hath on.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Effect it with some care, that he may prove

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: More fond on her than she upon her love:

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: And look thou meet me ere the first cock crow.

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Fear not, my lord, your servant shall do so.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Titania with her Train.

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: Come, now a roundel and a fairy song;

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: Then for the third part of a minute, hence;

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: Some to kill cankers in the musk-rose buds;

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: Some war with reremice for their leathern wings,

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: To make my small elves coats; and some keep back

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: The clamorous owl, that nightly hoots and wonders

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: At our quaint spirits. Sing me now asleep;

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: Then to your offices, and let me rest.

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: Fairies sing.

lines.speaker: FIRST FAIRY
lines.text: You spotted snakes with double tongue,

lines.speaker: FIRST FAIRY
lines.text: Thorny hedgehogs, be not seen;

lines.speaker: FIRST FAIRY
lines.text: Newts and blind-worms do no wrong,

lines.speaker: FIRST FAIRY
lines.text: Come not near our Fairy Queen:

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Philomel, with melody,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Sing in our sweet lullaby:

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Lulla, lulla, lullaby; lulla, lulla, lullaby.

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Never harm, nor spell, nor charm,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Come our lovely lady nigh;

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: So good night, with lullaby.

lines.speaker: FIRST FAIRY
lines.text: Weaving spiders, come not here;

lines.speaker: FIRST FAIRY
lines.text: Hence, you long-legg’d spinners, hence.

lines.speaker: FIRST FAIRY
lines.text: Beetles black, approach not near;

lines.speaker: FIRST FAIRY
lines.text: Worm nor snail do no offence.

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Philomel with melody, &c.

lines.speaker: SECOND FAIRY
lines.text: Hence away! Now all is well.

lines.speaker: SECOND FAIRY
lines.text: One aloof stand sentinel.
[_Exeunt Fairies. Titania sleeps._]
Enter Oberon.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: What thou seest when thou dost wake,
[_Squeezes the flower on  Titania’s eyelids._]

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Do it for thy true love take;

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Love and languish for his sake.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Be it ounce, or cat, or bear,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Pard, or boar with bristled hair,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: In thy eye that shall appear

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: When thou wak’st, it is thy dear.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Wake when some vile thing is near.
[_Exit._]
Enter Lysander and Hermia.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Fair love, you faint with wand’ring in the wood.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: And, to speak troth, I have forgot our way.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: We’ll rest us, Hermia, if you think it good,

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: And tarry for the comfort of the day.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Be it so, Lysander: find you out a bed,

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: For I upon this bank will rest my head.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: One turf shall serve as pillow for us both;

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: One heart, one bed, two bosoms, and one troth.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Nay, good Lysander; for my sake, my dear,

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Lie further off yet, do not lie so near.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: O take the sense, sweet, of my innocence!

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Love takes the meaning in love’s conference.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: I mean that my heart unto yours is knit,

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: So that but one heart we can make of it:

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Two bosoms interchainèd with an oath,

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: So then two bosoms and a single troth.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Then by your side no bed-room me deny;

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: For lying so, Hermia, I do not lie.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Lysander riddles very prettily.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Now much beshrew my manners and my pride,

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: If Hermia meant to say Lysander lied!

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: But, gentle friend, for love and courtesy

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Lie further off, in human modesty,

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Such separation as may well be said

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Becomes a virtuous bachelor and a maid,

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: So far be distant; and good night, sweet friend:

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Thy love ne’er alter till thy sweet life end!

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Amen, amen, to that fair prayer say I;

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: And then end life when I end loyalty!

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Here is my bed. Sleep give thee all his rest!

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: With half that wish the wisher’s eyes be pressed!
[_They sleep._]
Enter Puck.

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Through the forest have I gone,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: But Athenian found I none,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: On whose eyes I might approve

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: This flower’s force in stirring love.

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Night and silence! Who is here?

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Weeds of Athens he doth wear:

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: This is he, my master said,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Despisèd the Athenian maid;

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: And here the maiden, sleeping sound,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: On the dank and dirty ground.

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Pretty soul, she durst not lie

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Near this lack-love, this kill-courtesy.

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Churl, upon thy eyes I throw

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: All the power this charm doth owe;

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: When thou wak’st let love forbid

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Sleep his seat on thy eyelid.

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: So awake when I am gone;

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: For I must now to Oberon.
[_Exit._]
Enter Demetrius and Helena, running.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Stay, though thou kill me, sweet Demetrius.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: I charge thee, hence, and do not haunt me thus.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: O, wilt thou darkling leave me? Do not so.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Stay, on thy peril; I alone will go.
[_Exit Demetrius._]

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: O, I am out of breath in this fond chase!

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: The more my prayer, the lesser is my grace.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Happy is Hermia, wheresoe’er she lies,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: For she hath blessèd and attractive eyes.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: How came her eyes so bright? Not with salt tears.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: If so, my eyes are oftener wash’d than hers.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: No, no, I am as ugly as a bear,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: For beasts that meet me run away for fear:

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Therefore no marvel though Demetrius

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Do, as a monster, fly my presence thus.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: What wicked and dissembling glass of mine

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Made me compare with Hermia’s sphery eyne?

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: But who is here? Lysander, on the ground!

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Dead or asleep? I see no blood, no wound.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Lysander, if you live, good sir, awake.
[_Waking._]

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: And run through fire I will for thy sweet sake.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Transparent Helena! Nature shows art,

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: That through thy bosom makes me see thy heart.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Where is Demetrius? O, how fit a word

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Is that vile name to perish on my sword!

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Do not say so, Lysander, say not so.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: What though he love your Hermia? Lord, what though?

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Yet Hermia still loves you. Then be content.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Content with Hermia? No, I do repent

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: The tedious minutes I with her have spent.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Not Hermia, but Helena I love.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Who will not change a raven for a dove?

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: The will of man is by his reason sway’d,

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: And reason says you are the worthier maid.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Things growing are not ripe until their season;

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: So I, being young, till now ripe not to reason;

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: And touching now the point of human skill,

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Reason becomes the marshal to my will,

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: And leads me to your eyes, where I o’erlook

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Love’s stories, written in love’s richest book.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Wherefore was I to this keen mockery born?

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: When at your hands did I deserve this scorn?

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Is’t not enough, is’t not enough, young man,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: That I did never, no, nor never can

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Deserve a sweet look from Demetrius’ eye,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: But you must flout my insufficiency?

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Good troth, you do me wrong, good sooth, you do,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: In such disdainful manner me to woo.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: But fare you well; perforce I must confess,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: I thought you lord of more true gentleness.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: O, that a lady of one man refus’d,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Should of another therefore be abus’d!
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: She sees not Hermia. Hermia, sleep thou there,

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: And never mayst thou come Lysander near!

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: For, as a surfeit of the sweetest things

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: The deepest loathing to the stomach brings;

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Or as the heresies that men do leave

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Are hated most of those they did deceive;

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: So thou, my surfeit and my heresy,

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Of all be hated, but the most of me!

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: And, all my powers, address your love and might

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: To honour Helen, and to be her knight!
[_Exit._]
[_Starting._]

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Help me, Lysander, help me! Do thy best

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: To pluck this crawling serpent from my breast!

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Ay me, for pity! What a dream was here!

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Lysander, look how I do quake with fear.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Methought a serpent eat my heart away,

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: And you sat smiling at his cruel prey.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Lysander! What, removed? Lysander! lord!

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: What, out of hearing? Gone? No sound, no word?

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Alack, where are you? Speak, and if you hear;

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Speak, of all loves! I swoon almost with fear.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: No? Then I well perceive you are not nigh.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Either death or you I’ll find immediately.
[_Exit._]
The Queen of Fairies still lying asleep.
Enter Bottom, Quince, Snout, Starveling, Snug and Flute.

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: Are we all met?

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: Pat, pat; and here’s a marvellous convenient place for our rehearsal.

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: This green plot shall be our stage, this hawthorn brake our

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: tiring-house; and we will do it in action, as we will do it before the

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: Duke.

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: Peter Quince?

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: What sayest thou, bully Bottom?

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: There are things in this comedy of Pyramus and Thisbe that will never

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: please. First, Pyramus must draw a sword to kill himself; which the

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: ladies cannot abide. How answer you that?

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: SNOUT

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: By’r lakin, a parlous fear.

lines.speaker: STARVELING
lines.text: I believe we must leave the killing out, when all is done.

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: Not a whit; I have a device to make all well. Write me a prologue, and

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: let the prologue seem to say we will do no harm with our swords, and

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: that Pyramus is not killed indeed; and for the more better assurance,

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: tell them that I Pyramus am not Pyramus but Bottom the weaver. This

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: will put them out of fear.

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: Well, we will have such a prologue; and it shall be written in eight

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: and six.

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: No, make it two more; let it be written in eight and eight.

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: SNOUT

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: Will not the ladies be afeard of the lion?

lines.speaker: STARVELING
lines.text: I fear it, I promise you.

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: Masters, you ought to consider with yourselves, to bring in (God shield

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: us!) a lion among ladies is a most dreadful thing. For there is not a

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: more fearful wild-fowl than your lion living; and we ought to look to

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: it.

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: SNOUT

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: Therefore another prologue must tell he is not a lion.

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: Nay, you must name his name, and half his face must be seen through the

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: lion’s neck; and he himself must speak through, saying thus, or to the

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: same defect: ‘Ladies,’ or, ‘Fair ladies, I would wish you,’ or, ‘I

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: would request you,’ or, ’I would entreat you, not to fear, not to

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: tremble: my life for yours. If you think I come hither as a lion, it

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: were pity of my life. No, I am no such thing; I am a man as other men

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: are’: and there, indeed, let him name his name, and tell them plainly

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: he is Snug the joiner.

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: Well, it shall be so. But there is two hard things: that is, to bring

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: the moonlight into a chamber, for you know, Pyramus and Thisbe meet by

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: moonlight.

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: SNOUT

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: Doth the moon shine that night we play our play?

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: A calendar, a calendar! Look in the almanack; find out moonshine, find

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: out moonshine.

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: Yes, it doth shine that night.

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: Why, then may you leave a casement of the great chamber window, where

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: we play, open; and the moon may shine in at the casement.

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: Ay; or else one must come in with a bush of thorns and a lantern, and

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: say he comes to disfigure or to present the person of Moonshine. Then

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: there is another thing: we must have a wall in the great chamber; for

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: Pyramus and Thisbe, says the story, did talk through the chink of a

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: wall.

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: SNOUT

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: You can never bring in a wall. What say you, Bottom?

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: Some man or other must present Wall. And let him have some plaster, or

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: some loam, or some rough-cast about him, to signify wall; and let him

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: hold his fingers thus, and through that cranny shall Pyramus and Thisbe

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: whisper.

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: If that may be, then all is well. Come, sit down, every mother’s son,

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: and rehearse your parts. Pyramus, you begin: when you have spoken your

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: speech, enter into that brake; and so everyone according to his cue.
Enter Puck behind.

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: What hempen homespuns have we swaggering here,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: So near the cradle of the Fairy Queen?

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: What, a play toward? I’ll be an auditor;

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: An actor too perhaps, if I see cause.

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: Speak, Pyramus.—Thisbe, stand forth.

lines.speaker: PYRAMUS
lines.text: _Thisbe, the flowers of odious savours sweet_

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: Odours, odours.

lines.speaker: PYRAMUS
lines.text: _. . . odours savours sweet.

lines.speaker: PYRAMUS
lines.text: So hath thy breath, my dearest Thisbe dear.

lines.speaker: PYRAMUS
lines.text: But hark, a voice! Stay thou but here awhile,

lines.speaker: PYRAMUS
lines.text: And by and by I will to thee appear._
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: A stranger Pyramus than e’er played here!
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: THISBE
lines.text: Must I speak now?

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: Ay, marry, must you, For you must understand he goes but to see a noise

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: that he heard, and is to come again.

lines.speaker: THISBE
lines.text: _Most radiant Pyramus, most lily-white of hue,

lines.speaker: THISBE
lines.text: Of colour like the red rose on triumphant brier,

lines.speaker: THISBE
lines.text: Most brisky juvenal, and eke most lovely Jew,

lines.speaker: THISBE
lines.text: As true as truest horse, that yet would never tire,

lines.speaker: THISBE
lines.text: I’ll meet thee, Pyramus, at Ninny’s tomb._

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: Ninus’ tomb, man! Why, you must not speak that yet. That you answer to

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: Pyramus. You speak all your part at once, cues, and all.—Pyramus enter!

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: Your cue is past; it is ‘never tire.’

lines.speaker: THISBE
lines.text: O, _As true as truest horse, that yet would never tire._
Enter Puck and Bottom with an ass’s head.

lines.speaker: PYRAMUS
lines.text: _If I were fair, Thisbe, I were only thine._

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: O monstrous! O strange! We are haunted. Pray, masters, fly, masters!

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: Help!
[_Exeunt Clowns._]

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: I’ll follow you. I’ll lead you about a round,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Through bog, through bush, through brake, through brier;

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Sometime a horse I’ll be, sometime a hound,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: A hog, a headless bear, sometime a fire;

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: And neigh, and bark, and grunt, and roar, and burn,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Like horse, hound, hog, bear, fire, at every turn.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: Why do they run away? This is a knavery of them to make me afeard.
Enter Snout.

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: SNOUT

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: O Bottom, thou art changed! What do I see on thee?

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: What do you see? You see an ass-head of your own, do you?
[_Exit Snout._]
Enter Quince.

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: Bless thee, Bottom! bless thee! Thou art translated.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: I see their knavery. This is to make an ass of me, to fright me, if

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: they could. But I will not stir from this place, do what they can. I

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: will walk up and down here, and I will sing, that they shall hear I am

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: not afraid.
[_Sings._]

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: The ousel cock, so black of hue,

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: With orange-tawny bill,

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: The throstle with his note so true,

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: The wren with little quill.
[_Waking._]

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: What angel wakes me from my flowery bed?
[_Sings._]

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: The finch, the sparrow, and the lark,

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: The plain-song cuckoo gray,

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: Whose note full many a man doth mark,

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: And dares not answer nay.

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: for, indeed, who would set his wit to so foolish a bird? Who would give

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: a bird the lie, though he cry ‘cuckoo’ never so?

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: I pray thee, gentle mortal, sing again.

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: Mine ear is much enamour’d of thy note.

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: So is mine eye enthrallèd to thy shape;

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: And thy fair virtue’s force perforce doth move me,

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: On the first view, to say, to swear, I love thee.

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: Methinks, mistress, you should have little reason for that. And yet, to

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: say the truth, reason and love keep little company together nowadays.

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: The more the pity that some honest neighbours will not make them

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: friends. Nay, I can gleek upon occasion.

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: Thou art as wise as thou art beautiful.

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: Not so, neither; but if I had wit enough to get out of this wood, I

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: have enough to serve mine own turn.

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: Out of this wood do not desire to go.

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: Thou shalt remain here whether thou wilt or no.

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: I am a spirit of no common rate.

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: The summer still doth tend upon my state;

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: And I do love thee: therefore, go with me.

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: I’ll give thee fairies to attend on thee;

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: And they shall fetch thee jewels from the deep,

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: And sing, while thou on pressèd flowers dost sleep.

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: And I will purge thy mortal grossness so

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: That thou shalt like an airy spirit go.—

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: Peaseblossom! Cobweb! Moth! and Mustardseed!
Enter four Fairies.

lines.speaker: PEASEBLOSSOM
lines.text: Ready.

lines.speaker: COBWEB
lines.text: And I.

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: And I.

lines.speaker: MUSTARDSEED
lines.text: And I.

lines.speaker: ALL
lines.text: Where shall we go?

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: Be kind and courteous to this gentleman;

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: Hop in his walks and gambol in his eyes;

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: Feed him with apricocks and dewberries,

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: With purple grapes, green figs, and mulberries;

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: The honey-bags steal from the humble-bees,

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: And for night-tapers, crop their waxen thighs,

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: And light them at the fiery glow-worm’s eyes,

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: To have my love to bed and to arise;

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: And pluck the wings from painted butterflies,

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: To fan the moonbeams from his sleeping eyes.

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: Nod to him, elves, and do him courtesies.

lines.speaker: PEASEBLOSSOM
lines.text: Hail, mortal!

lines.speaker: COBWEB
lines.text: Hail!

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: Hail!

lines.speaker: MUSTARDSEED
lines.text: Hail!

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: I cry your worships mercy, heartily.—I beseech your worship’s name.

lines.speaker: COBWEB
lines.text: Cobweb.

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: I shall desire you of more acquaintance, good Master Cobweb. If I cut

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: my finger, I shall make bold with you.—Your name, honest gentleman?

lines.speaker: PEASEBLOSSOM
lines.text: Peaseblossom.

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: I pray you, commend me to Mistress Squash, your mother, and to Master

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: Peascod, your father. Good Master Peaseblossom, I shall desire you of

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: more acquaintance too.—Your name, I beseech you, sir?

lines.speaker: MUSTARDSEED
lines.text: Mustardseed.

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: Good Master Mustardseed, I know your patience well. That same cowardly

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: giant-like ox-beef hath devoured many a gentleman of your house. I

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: promise you, your kindred hath made my eyes water ere now. I desire you

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: of more acquaintance, good Master Mustardseed.

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: Come, wait upon him; lead him to my bower.

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: The moon, methinks, looks with a watery eye,

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: And when she weeps, weeps every little flower,

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: Lamenting some enforced chastity.

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: Tie up my love’s tongue, bring him silently.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Oberon.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: I wonder if Titania be awak’d;

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Then, what it was that next came in her eye,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Which she must dote on in extremity.
Enter Puck.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Here comes my messenger. How now, mad spirit?

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: What night-rule now about this haunted grove?

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: My mistress with a monster is in love.

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Near to her close and consecrated bower,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: While she was in her dull and sleeping hour,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: A crew of patches, rude mechanicals,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: That work for bread upon Athenian stalls,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Were met together to rehearse a play

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Intended for great Theseus’ nuptial day.

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: The shallowest thick-skin of that barren sort

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Who Pyramus presented in their sport,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Forsook his scene and enter’d in a brake.

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: When I did him at this advantage take,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: An ass’s nole I fixed on his head.

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Anon, his Thisbe must be answerèd,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: And forth my mimic comes. When they him spy,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: As wild geese that the creeping fowler eye,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Or russet-pated choughs, many in sort,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Rising and cawing at the gun’s report,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Sever themselves and madly sweep the sky,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: So at his sight away his fellows fly,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: And at our stamp, here o’er and o’er one falls;

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: He murder cries, and help from Athens calls.

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Their sense thus weak, lost with their fears, thus strong,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Made senseless things begin to do them wrong;

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: For briers and thorns at their apparel snatch;

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Some sleeves, some hats, from yielders all things catch.

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: I led them on in this distracted fear,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: And left sweet Pyramus translated there.

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: When in that moment, so it came to pass,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Titania wak’d, and straightway lov’d an ass.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: This falls out better than I could devise.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: But hast thou yet latch’d the Athenian’s eyes

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: With the love-juice, as I did bid thee do?

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: I took him sleeping—that is finish’d too—

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: And the Athenian woman by his side,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: That, when he wak’d, of force she must be ey’d.
Enter Demetrius and Hermia.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Stand close. This is the same Athenian.

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: This is the woman, but not this the man.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: O why rebuke you him that loves you so?

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Lay breath so bitter on your bitter foe.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Now I but chide, but I should use thee worse,

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: For thou, I fear, hast given me cause to curse.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: If thou hast slain Lysander in his sleep,

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Being o’er shoes in blood, plunge in the deep,

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: And kill me too.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: The sun was not so true unto the day

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: As he to me. Would he have stol’n away

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: From sleeping Hermia? I’ll believe as soon

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: This whole earth may be bor’d, and that the moon

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: May through the centre creep and so displease

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Her brother’s noontide with th’ Antipodes.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: It cannot be but thou hast murder’d him.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: So should a murderer look, so dead, so grim.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: So should the murder’d look, and so should I,

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Pierc’d through the heart with your stern cruelty.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Yet you, the murderer, look as bright, as clear,

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: As yonder Venus in her glimmering sphere.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: What’s this to my Lysander? Where is he?

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Ah, good Demetrius, wilt thou give him me?

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: I had rather give his carcass to my hounds.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Out, dog! Out, cur! Thou driv’st me past the bounds

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Of maiden’s patience. Hast thou slain him, then?

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Henceforth be never number’d among men!

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: O once tell true; tell true, even for my sake!

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Durst thou have look’d upon him, being awake,

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: And hast thou kill’d him sleeping? O brave touch!

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Could not a worm, an adder, do so much?

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: An adder did it; for with doubler tongue

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Than thine, thou serpent, never adder stung.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: You spend your passion on a mispris’d mood:

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: I am not guilty of Lysander’s blood;

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Nor is he dead, for aught that I can tell.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: I pray thee, tell me then that he is well.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: And if I could, what should I get therefore?

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: A privilege never to see me more.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: And from thy hated presence part I so:

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: See me no more, whether he be dead or no.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: There is no following her in this fierce vein.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Here, therefore, for a while I will remain.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: So sorrow’s heaviness doth heavier grow

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: For debt that bankrupt sleep doth sorrow owe;

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Which now in some slight measure it will pay,

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: If for his tender here I make some stay.
[_Lies down._]

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: What hast thou done? Thou hast mistaken quite,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: And laid the love-juice on some true-love’s sight.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Of thy misprision must perforce ensue

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Some true love turn’d, and not a false turn’d true.

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Then fate o’er-rules, that, one man holding troth,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: A million fail, confounding oath on oath.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: About the wood go swifter than the wind,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: And Helena of Athens look thou find.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: All fancy-sick she is, and pale of cheer

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: With sighs of love, that costs the fresh blood dear.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: By some illusion see thou bring her here;

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: I’ll charm his eyes against she do appear.

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: I go, I go; look how I go,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Swifter than arrow from the Tartar’s bow.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Flower of this purple dye,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Hit with Cupid’s archery,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Sink in apple of his eye.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: When his love he doth espy,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Let her shine as gloriously

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: As the Venus of the sky.—

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: When thou wak’st, if she be by,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Beg of her for remedy.
Enter Puck.

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Captain of our fairy band,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Helena is here at hand,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: And the youth mistook by me,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Pleading for a lover’s fee.

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Shall we their fond pageant see?

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Lord, what fools these mortals be!

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Stand aside. The noise they make

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Will cause Demetrius to awake.

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Then will two at once woo one.

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: That must needs be sport alone;

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: And those things do best please me

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: That befall prepost’rously.
Enter Lysander and Helena.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Why should you think that I should woo in scorn?

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Scorn and derision never come in tears.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Look when I vow, I weep; and vows so born,

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: In their nativity all truth appears.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: How can these things in me seem scorn to you,

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Bearing the badge of faith, to prove them true?

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: You do advance your cunning more and more.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: When truth kills truth, O devilish-holy fray!

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: These vows are Hermia’s: will you give her o’er?

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Weigh oath with oath, and you will nothing weigh:

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Your vows to her and me, put in two scales,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Will even weigh; and both as light as tales.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: I had no judgment when to her I swore.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Nor none, in my mind, now you give her o’er.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Demetrius loves her, and he loves not you.
[_Waking._]

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: O Helen, goddess, nymph, perfect, divine!

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: To what, my love, shall I compare thine eyne?

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Crystal is muddy. O how ripe in show

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Thy lips, those kissing cherries, tempting grow!

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: That pure congealèd white, high Taurus’ snow,

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Fann’d with the eastern wind, turns to a crow

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: When thou hold’st up thy hand. O, let me kiss

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: This princess of pure white, this seal of bliss!

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: O spite! O hell! I see you all are bent

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: To set against me for your merriment.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: If you were civil, and knew courtesy,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: You would not do me thus much injury.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Can you not hate me, as I know you do,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: But you must join in souls to mock me too?

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: If you were men, as men you are in show,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: You would not use a gentle lady so;

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: To vow, and swear, and superpraise my parts,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: When I am sure you hate me with your hearts.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: You both are rivals, and love Hermia;

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: And now both rivals, to mock Helena.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: A trim exploit, a manly enterprise,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: To conjure tears up in a poor maid’s eyes

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: With your derision! None of noble sort

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Would so offend a virgin, and extort

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: A poor soul’s patience, all to make you sport.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: You are unkind, Demetrius; be not so,

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: For you love Hermia; this you know I know.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: And here, with all good will, with all my heart,

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: In Hermia’s love I yield you up my part;

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: And yours of Helena to me bequeath,

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Whom I do love and will do till my death.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Never did mockers waste more idle breath.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Lysander, keep thy Hermia; I will none.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: If e’er I lov’d her, all that love is gone.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: My heart to her but as guest-wise sojourn’d;

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: And now to Helen is it home return’d,

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: There to remain.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Helen, it is not so.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Disparage not the faith thou dost not know,

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Lest to thy peril thou aby it dear.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Look where thy love comes; yonder is thy dear.
Enter Hermia.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Dark night, that from the eye his function takes,

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: The ear more quick of apprehension makes;

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Wherein it doth impair the seeing sense,

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: It pays the hearing double recompense.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Thou art not by mine eye, Lysander, found;

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Mine ear, I thank it, brought me to thy sound.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: But why unkindly didst thou leave me so?

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Why should he stay whom love doth press to go?

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: What love could press Lysander from my side?

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Lysander’s love, that would not let him bide,

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Fair Helena, who more engilds the night

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Than all yon fiery oes and eyes of light.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Why seek’st thou me? Could not this make thee know

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: The hate I bare thee made me leave thee so?

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: You speak not as you think; it cannot be.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Lo, she is one of this confederacy!

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Now I perceive they have conjoin’d all three

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: To fashion this false sport in spite of me.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Injurious Hermia, most ungrateful maid!

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Have you conspir’d, have you with these contriv’d,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: To bait me with this foul derision?

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Is all the counsel that we two have shar’d,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: The sisters’ vows, the hours that we have spent,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: When we have chid the hasty-footed time

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: For parting us—O, is all forgot?

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: All school-days’ friendship, childhood innocence?

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: We, Hermia, like two artificial gods,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Have with our needles created both one flower,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Both on one sampler, sitting on one cushion,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Both warbling of one song, both in one key,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: As if our hands, our sides, voices, and minds,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Had been incorporate. So we grew together,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Like to a double cherry, seeming parted,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: But yet a union in partition,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Two lovely berries moulded on one stem;

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: So, with two seeming bodies, but one heart;

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Two of the first, like coats in heraldry,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Due but to one, and crownèd with one crest.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: And will you rent our ancient love asunder,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: To join with men in scorning your poor friend?

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: It is not friendly, ’tis not maidenly.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Our sex, as well as I, may chide you for it,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Though I alone do feel the injury.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: I am amazèd at your passionate words:

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: I scorn you not; it seems that you scorn me.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Have you not set Lysander, as in scorn,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: To follow me, and praise my eyes and face?

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: And made your other love, Demetrius,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Who even but now did spurn me with his foot,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: To call me goddess, nymph, divine and rare,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Precious, celestial? Wherefore speaks he this

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: To her he hates? And wherefore doth Lysander

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Deny your love, so rich within his soul,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: And tender me, forsooth, affection,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: But by your setting on, by your consent?

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: What though I be not so in grace as you,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: So hung upon with love, so fortunate,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: But miserable most, to love unlov’d?

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: This you should pity rather than despise.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: I understand not what you mean by this.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Ay, do. Persever, counterfeit sad looks,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Make mouths upon me when I turn my back,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Wink each at other; hold the sweet jest up.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: This sport, well carried, shall be chronicled.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: If you have any pity, grace, or manners,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: You would not make me such an argument.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: But fare ye well. ’Tis partly my own fault,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Which death, or absence, soon shall remedy.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Stay, gentle Helena; hear my excuse;

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: My love, my life, my soul, fair Helena!

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: O excellent!

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Sweet, do not scorn her so.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: If she cannot entreat, I can compel.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Thou canst compel no more than she entreat;

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Thy threats have no more strength than her weak prayers.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Helen, I love thee, by my life I do;

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: I swear by that which I will lose for thee

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: To prove him false that says I love thee not.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: I say I love thee more than he can do.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: If thou say so, withdraw, and prove it too.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Quick, come.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Lysander, whereto tends all this?

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Away, you Ethiope!

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: No, no. He will

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Seem to break loose. Take on as you would follow,

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: But yet come not. You are a tame man, go!

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Hang off, thou cat, thou burr! Vile thing, let loose,

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Or I will shake thee from me like a serpent.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Why are you grown so rude? What change is this,

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Sweet love?

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Thy love? Out, tawny Tartar, out!

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Out, loathèd medicine! O hated potion, hence!

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Do you not jest?

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Yes, sooth, and so do you.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Demetrius, I will keep my word with thee.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: I would I had your bond; for I perceive

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: A weak bond holds you; I’ll not trust your word.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: What, should I hurt her, strike her, kill her dead?

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Although I hate her, I’ll not harm her so.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: What, can you do me greater harm than hate?

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Hate me? Wherefore? O me! what news, my love?

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Am not I Hermia? Are not you Lysander?

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: I am as fair now as I was erewhile.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Since night you lov’d me; yet since night you left me.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Why then, you left me—O, the gods forbid!—

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: In earnest, shall I say?

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Ay, by my life;

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: And never did desire to see thee more.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Therefore be out of hope, of question, of doubt;

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Be certain, nothing truer; ’tis no jest

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: That I do hate thee and love Helena.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: O me! You juggler! You cankerblossom!

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: You thief of love! What! have you come by night

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: And stol’n my love’s heart from him?

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Fine, i’ faith!

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Have you no modesty, no maiden shame,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: No touch of bashfulness? What, will you tear

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Impatient answers from my gentle tongue?

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Fie, fie, you counterfeit, you puppet, you!

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Puppet! Why so? Ay, that way goes the game.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Now I perceive that she hath made compare

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Between our statures; she hath urg’d her height;

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: And with her personage, her tall personage,

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Her height, forsooth, she hath prevail’d with him.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: And are you grown so high in his esteem

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Because I am so dwarfish and so low?

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: How low am I, thou painted maypole? Speak,

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: How low am I? I am not yet so low

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: But that my nails can reach unto thine eyes.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: I pray you, though you mock me, gentlemen,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Let her not hurt me. I was never curst;

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: I have no gift at all in shrewishness;

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: I am a right maid for my cowardice;

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Let her not strike me. You perhaps may think,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Because she is something lower than myself,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: That I can match her.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Lower! Hark, again.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Good Hermia, do not be so bitter with me.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: I evermore did love you, Hermia,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Did ever keep your counsels, never wrong’d you,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Save that, in love unto Demetrius,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: I told him of your stealth unto this wood.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: He follow’d you; for love I follow’d him;

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: But he hath chid me hence, and threaten’d me

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: To strike me, spurn me, nay, to kill me too:

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: And now, so you will let me quiet go,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: To Athens will I bear my folly back,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: And follow you no further. Let me go:

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: You see how simple and how fond I am.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Why, get you gone. Who is’t that hinders you?

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: A foolish heart that I leave here behind.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: What! with Lysander?

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: With Demetrius.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Be not afraid; she shall not harm thee, Helena.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: No, sir, she shall not, though you take her part.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: O, when she’s angry, she is keen and shrewd.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: She was a vixen when she went to school,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: And though she be but little, she is fierce.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Little again! Nothing but low and little?

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Why will you suffer her to flout me thus?

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Let me come to her.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Get you gone, you dwarf;

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: You minimus, of hind’ring knot-grass made;

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: You bead, you acorn.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: You are too officious

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: In her behalf that scorns your services.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Let her alone. Speak not of Helena;

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Take not her part; for if thou dost intend

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Never so little show of love to her,

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Thou shalt aby it.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Now she holds me not.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Now follow, if thou dar’st, to try whose right,

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Of thine or mine, is most in Helena.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Follow! Nay, I’ll go with thee, cheek by jole.
[_Exeunt Lysander and Demetrius._]

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: You, mistress, all this coil is long of you.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Nay, go not back.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: I will not trust you, I,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Nor longer stay in your curst company.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Your hands than mine are quicker for a fray.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: My legs are longer though, to run away.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: I am amaz’d, and know not what to say.
[_Exit, pursuing Helena._]

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: This is thy negligence: still thou mistak’st,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Or else commit’st thy knaveries willfully.

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Believe me, king of shadows, I mistook.

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Did not you tell me I should know the man

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: By the Athenian garments he had on?

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: And so far blameless proves my enterprise

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: That I have ’nointed an Athenian’s eyes:

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: And so far am I glad it so did sort,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: As this their jangling I esteem a sport.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Thou seest these lovers seek a place to fight.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Hie therefore, Robin, overcast the night;

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: The starry welkin cover thou anon

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: With drooping fog, as black as Acheron,

lines.speaker: OBERON
