lines.text: And lead these testy rivals so astray

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: As one come not within another’s way.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Like to Lysander sometime frame thy tongue,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Then stir Demetrius up with bitter wrong;

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: And sometime rail thou like Demetrius.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: And from each other look thou lead them thus,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Till o’er their brows death-counterfeiting sleep

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: With leaden legs and batty wings doth creep.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Then crush this herb into Lysander’s eye,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Whose liquor hath this virtuous property,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: To take from thence all error with his might

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: And make his eyeballs roll with wonted sight.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: When they next wake, all this derision

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Shall seem a dream and fruitless vision;

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: And back to Athens shall the lovers wend,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: With league whose date till death shall never end.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Whiles I in this affair do thee employ,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: I’ll to my queen, and beg her Indian boy;

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: And then I will her charmèd eye release

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: From monster’s view, and all things shall be peace.

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: My fairy lord, this must be done with haste,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: For night’s swift dragons cut the clouds full fast;

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: And yonder shines Aurora’s harbinger,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: At whose approach, ghosts wandering here and there

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Troop home to churchyards. Damnèd spirits all,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: That in cross-ways and floods have burial,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Already to their wormy beds are gone;

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: For fear lest day should look their shames upon,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: They wilfully themselves exile from light,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: And must for aye consort with black-brow’d night.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: But we are spirits of another sort:

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: I with the morning’s love have oft made sport;

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: And, like a forester, the groves may tread

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Even till the eastern gate, all fiery-red,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Opening on Neptune with fair blessèd beams,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Turns into yellow gold his salt-green streams.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: But, notwithstanding, haste, make no delay.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: We may effect this business yet ere day.
[_Exit Oberon._]

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Up and down, up and down,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: I will lead them up and down.

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: I am fear’d in field and town.

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Goblin, lead them up and down.

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Here comes one.
Enter Lysander.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Where art thou, proud Demetrius? Speak thou now.

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Here, villain, drawn and ready. Where art thou?

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: I will be with thee straight.

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Follow me then to plainer ground.
[_Exit Lysander as following the voice._]
Enter Demetrius.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Lysander, speak again.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Thou runaway, thou coward, art thou fled?

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Speak. In some bush? Where dost thou hide thy head?

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Thou coward, art thou bragging to the stars,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Telling the bushes that thou look’st for wars,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: And wilt not come? Come, recreant, come, thou child!

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: I’ll whip thee with a rod. He is defil’d

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: That draws a sword on thee.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Yea, art thou there?

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Follow my voice; we’ll try no manhood here.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Lysander.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: He goes before me, and still dares me on;

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: When I come where he calls, then he is gone.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: The villain is much lighter-heel’d than I:

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: I follow’d fast, but faster he did fly,

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: That fallen am I in dark uneven way,

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: And here will rest me.  Come, thou gentle day!
[_Lies down._]

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: For if but once thou show me thy grey light,

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: I’ll find Demetrius, and revenge this spite.
[_Sleeps._]
Enter Puck and Demetrius.

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Ho, ho, ho! Coward, why com’st thou not?

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Abide me, if thou dar’st; for well I wot

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Thou runn’st before me, shifting every place,

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: And dar’st not stand, nor look me in the face.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Where art thou?

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Come hither; I am here.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Nay, then, thou mock’st me. Thou shalt buy this dear

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: If ever I thy face by daylight see:

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Now go thy way. Faintness constraineth me

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: To measure out my length on this cold bed.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: By day’s approach look to be visited.
[_Lies down and sleeps._]
Enter Helena.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: O weary night, O long and tedious night,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Abate thy hours! Shine, comforts, from the east,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: That I may back to Athens by daylight,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: From these that my poor company detest.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: And sleep, that sometimes shuts up sorrow’s eye,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Steal me awhile from mine own company.
[_Sleeps._]

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Yet but three? Come one more.

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Two of both kinds makes up four.

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Here she comes, curst and sad.

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Cupid is a knavish lad

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Thus to make poor females mad.
Enter Hermia.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Never so weary, never so in woe,

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Bedabbled with the dew, and torn with briers,

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: I can no further crawl, no further go;

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: My legs can keep no pace with my desires.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Here will I rest me till the break of day.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Heavens shield Lysander, if they mean a fray!
[_Lies down._]

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: On the ground

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Sleep sound.

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: I’ll apply

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: To your eye,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Gentle lover, remedy.
[_Squeezing the juice on Lysander’s eye._]

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: When thou wak’st,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Thou tak’st

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: True delight

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: In the sight

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Of thy former lady’s eye.

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: And the country proverb known,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: That every man should take his own,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: In your waking shall be shown:

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Jack shall have Jill;

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Nought shall go ill;

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: The man shall have his mare again, and all shall be well.
[_Exit Puck._]
Lysander, Demetrius, Helena and Hermia still asleep.
Enter Titania and Bottom; Peaseblossom, Cobweb, Moth, Mustardseed and other Fairies attending; Oberon behind, unseen.

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: Come, sit thee down upon this flowery bed,

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: While I thy amiable cheeks do coy,

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: And stick musk-roses in thy sleek smooth head,

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: And kiss thy fair large ears, my gentle joy.

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: Where’s Peaseblossom?

lines.speaker: PEASEBLOSSOM
lines.text: Ready.

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: Scratch my head, Peaseblossom. Where’s Monsieur Cobweb?

lines.speaker: COBWEB
lines.text: Ready.

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: Monsieur Cobweb; good monsieur, get you your weapons in your hand and

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: kill me a red-hipped humble-bee on the top of a thistle; and, good

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: monsieur, bring me the honey-bag. Do not fret yourself too much in the

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: action, monsieur; and, good monsieur, have a care the honey-bag break

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: not; I would be loath to have you overflown with a honey-bag, signior.

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: Where’s Monsieur Mustardseed?

lines.speaker: MUSTARDSEED
lines.text: Ready.

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: Give me your neaf, Monsieur Mustardseed. Pray you, leave your courtesy,

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: good monsieur.

lines.speaker: MUSTARDSEED
lines.text: What’s your will?

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: Nothing, good monsieur, but to help Cavalery Cobweb to scratch. I must

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: to the barber’s, monsieur, for methinks I am marvellous hairy about the

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: face; and I am such a tender ass, if my hair do but tickle me, I must

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: scratch.

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: What, wilt thou hear some music, my sweet love?

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: I have a reasonable good ear in music. Let us have the tongs and the

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: bones.

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: Or say, sweet love, what thou desirest to eat.

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: Truly, a peck of provender; I could munch your good dry oats. Methinks

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: I have a great desire to a bottle of hay: good hay, sweet hay, hath no

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: fellow.

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: I have a venturous fairy that shall seek

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: The squirrel’s hoard, and fetch thee new nuts.

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: I had rather have a handful or two of dried peas. But, I pray you, let

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: none of your people stir me; I have an exposition of sleep come upon

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: me.

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: Sleep thou, and I will wind thee in my arms.

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: Fairies, be gone, and be all ways away.

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: So doth the woodbine the sweet honeysuckle

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: Gently entwist, the female ivy so

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: Enrings the barky fingers of the elm.

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: O, how I love thee! How I dote on thee!
[_They sleep._]

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: Oberon advances. Enter Puck.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Welcome, good Robin. Seest thou this sweet sight?

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Her dotage now I do begin to pity.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: For, meeting her of late behind the wood,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Seeking sweet favours for this hateful fool,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: I did upbraid her and fall out with her:

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: For she his hairy temples then had rounded

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: With coronet of fresh and fragrant flowers;

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: And that same dew, which sometime on the buds

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Was wont to swell like round and orient pearls,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Stood now within the pretty flouriets’ eyes,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Like tears that did their own disgrace bewail.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: When I had at my pleasure taunted her,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: And she in mild terms begg’d my patience,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: I then did ask of her her changeling child;

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Which straight she gave me, and her fairy sent

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: To bear him to my bower in fairyland.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: And now I have the boy, I will undo

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: This hateful imperfection of her eyes.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: And, gentle Puck, take this transformèd scalp

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: From off the head of this Athenian swain,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: That he awaking when the other do,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: May all to Athens back again repair,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: And think no more of this night’s accidents

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: But as the fierce vexation of a dream.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: But first I will release the Fairy Queen.
[_Touching her eyes with an herb._]

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Be as thou wast wont to be;

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: See as thou was wont to see.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Dian’s bud o’er Cupid’s flower

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Hath such force and blessed power.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Now, my Titania, wake you, my sweet queen.

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: My Oberon, what visions have I seen!

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: Methought I was enamour’d of an ass.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: There lies your love.

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: How came these things to pass?

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: O, how mine eyes do loathe his visage now!

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Silence awhile.—Robin, take off this head.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Titania, music call; and strike more dead

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Than common sleep, of all these five the sense.

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: Music, ho, music, such as charmeth sleep.

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Now when thou wak’st, with thine own fool’s eyes peep.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Sound, music.
[_Still music._]

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Come, my queen, take hands with me,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: And rock the ground whereon these sleepers be.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Now thou and I are new in amity,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: And will tomorrow midnight solemnly

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Dance in Duke Theseus’ house triumphantly,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: And bless it to all fair prosperity:

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: There shall the pairs of faithful lovers be

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Wedded, with Theseus, all in jollity.

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Fairy king, attend and mark.

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: I do hear the morning lark.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Then, my queen, in silence sad,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Trip we after night’s shade.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: We the globe can compass soon,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Swifter than the wand’ring moon.

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: Come, my lord, and in our flight,

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: Tell me how it came this night

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: That I sleeping here was found

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: With these mortals on the ground.
[_Exeunt. Horns sound within._]
Enter Theseus, Hippolyta, Egeus and Train.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Go, one of you, find out the forester;

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: For now our observation is perform’d;

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: And since we have the vaward of the day,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: My love shall hear the music of my hounds.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Uncouple in the western valley; let them go.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Dispatch I say, and find the forester.
[_Exit an Attendant._]

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: We will, fair queen, up to the mountain’s top,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: And mark the musical confusion

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Of hounds and echo in conjunction.

lines.speaker: HIPPOLYTA
lines.text: I was with Hercules and Cadmus once,

lines.speaker: HIPPOLYTA
lines.text: When in a wood of Crete they bay’d the bear

lines.speaker: HIPPOLYTA
lines.text: With hounds of Sparta. Never did I hear

lines.speaker: HIPPOLYTA
lines.text: Such gallant chiding; for, besides the groves,

lines.speaker: HIPPOLYTA
lines.text: The skies, the fountains, every region near

lines.speaker: HIPPOLYTA
lines.text: Seem’d all one mutual cry. I never heard

lines.speaker: HIPPOLYTA
lines.text: So musical a discord, such sweet thunder.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: My hounds are bred out of the Spartan kind,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: So flew’d, so sanded; and their heads are hung

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: With ears that sweep away the morning dew;

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Crook-knee’d and dewlap’d like Thessalian bulls;

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Slow in pursuit, but match’d in mouth like bells,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Each under each. A cry more tuneable

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Was never holla’d to, nor cheer’d with horn,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: In Crete, in Sparta, nor in Thessaly.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Judge when you hear.—But, soft, what nymphs are these?

lines.speaker: EGEUS
lines.text: My lord, this is my daughter here asleep,

lines.speaker: EGEUS
lines.text: And this Lysander; this Demetrius is;

lines.speaker: EGEUS
lines.text: This Helena, old Nedar’s Helena:

lines.speaker: EGEUS
lines.text: I wonder of their being here together.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: No doubt they rose up early to observe

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: The rite of May; and, hearing our intent,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Came here in grace of our solemnity.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: But speak, Egeus; is not this the day

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: That Hermia should give answer of her choice?

lines.speaker: EGEUS
lines.text: It is, my lord.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Go, bid the huntsmen wake them with their horns.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Horns, and shout within. Demetrius, Lysander, Hermia and Helena wake

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: and start up.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Good morrow, friends. Saint Valentine is past.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Begin these wood-birds but to couple now?

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Pardon, my lord.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: He and the rest kneel to  Theseus.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: I pray you all, stand up.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: I know you two are rival enemies.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: How comes this gentle concord in the world,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: That hatred is so far from jealousy

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: To sleep by hate, and fear no enmity?

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: My lord, I shall reply amazedly,

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Half sleep, half waking; but as yet, I swear,

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: I cannot truly say how I came here.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: But, as I think (for truly would I speak)

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: And now I do bethink me, so it is:

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: I came with Hermia hither. Our intent

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Was to be gone from Athens, where we might be

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Without the peril of the Athenian law.

lines.speaker: EGEUS
lines.text: Enough, enough, my lord; you have enough.

lines.speaker: EGEUS
lines.text: I beg the law, the law upon his head.

lines.speaker: EGEUS
lines.text: They would have stol’n away, they would, Demetrius,

lines.speaker: EGEUS
lines.text: Thereby to have defeated you and me:

lines.speaker: EGEUS
lines.text: You of your wife, and me of my consent,

lines.speaker: EGEUS
lines.text: Of my consent that she should be your wife.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: My lord, fair Helen told me of their stealth,

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Of this their purpose hither to this wood;

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: And I in fury hither follow’d them,

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Fair Helena in fancy following me.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: But, my good lord, I wot not by what power,

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: (But by some power it is) my love to Hermia,

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Melted as the snow, seems to me now

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: As the remembrance of an idle gaud

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Which in my childhood I did dote upon;

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: And all the faith, the virtue of my heart,

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: The object and the pleasure of mine eye,

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Is only Helena. To her, my lord,

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Was I betroth’d ere I saw Hermia.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: But like a sickness did I loathe this food.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: But, as in health, come to my natural taste,

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Now I do wish it, love it, long for it,

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: And will for evermore be true to it.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Fair lovers, you are fortunately met.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Of this discourse we more will hear anon.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Egeus, I will overbear your will;

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: For in the temple, by and by with us,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: These couples shall eternally be knit.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: And, for the morning now is something worn,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Our purpos’d hunting shall be set aside.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Away with us to Athens. Three and three,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: We’ll hold a feast in great solemnity.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Come, Hippolyta.
[_Exeunt Theseus, Hippolyta, Egeus and Train._]

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: These things seem small and undistinguishable,

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Like far-off mountains turnèd into clouds.

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Methinks I see these things with parted eye,

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: When everything seems double.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: So methinks.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: And I have found Demetrius like a jewel,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Mine own, and not mine own.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Are you sure

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: That we are awake? It seems to me

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: That yet we sleep, we dream. Do not you think

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: The Duke was here, and bid us follow him?

lines.speaker: HERMIA
lines.text: Yea, and my father.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: And Hippolyta.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: And he did bid us follow to the temple.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Why, then, we are awake: let’s follow him,

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: And by the way let us recount our dreams.
[_Exeunt._]
[_Waking._]

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: When my cue comes, call me, and I will answer. My next is

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: ‘Most fair Pyramus.’ Heigh-ho! Peter Quince! Flute, the bellows-mender!

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: Snout, the tinker! Starveling! God’s my life! Stol’n hence, and left me

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: asleep! I have had a most rare vision. I have had a dream, past the wit

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: of man to say what dream it was. Man is but an ass if he go about to

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: expound this dream. Methought I was—there is no man can tell what.

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: Methought I was, and methought I had—but man is but a patched fool if

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: he will offer to say what methought I had. The eye of man hath not

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: heard, the ear of man hath not seen, man’s hand is not able to taste,

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: his tongue to conceive, nor his heart to report, what my dream was. I

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: will get Peter Quince to write a ballad of this dream: it shall be

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: called ‘Bottom’s Dream’, because it hath no bottom; and I will sing it

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: in the latter end of a play, before the Duke. Peradventure, to make it

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: the more gracious, I shall sing it at her death.
[_Exit._]

scenes.setting: Athens. A Room in Quince’s House

lines.text: Enter Quince, Flute, Snout and Starveling.

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: Have you sent to Bottom’s house? Is he come home yet?

lines.speaker: STARVELING
lines.text: He cannot be heard of. Out of doubt he is transported.

lines.speaker: FLUTE
lines.text: If he come not, then the play is marred. It goes not forward, doth it?

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: It is not possible. You have not a man in all Athens able to discharge

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: Pyramus but he.

lines.speaker: FLUTE
lines.text: No, he hath simply the best wit of any handicraft man in Athens.

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: Yea, and the best person too, and he is a very paramour for a sweet

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: voice.

lines.speaker: FLUTE
lines.text: You must say paragon. A paramour is, God bless us, a thing of naught.
Enter Snug.

lines.speaker: FLUTE
lines.text: SNUG

lines.speaker: FLUTE
lines.text: Masters, the Duke is coming from the temple, and there is two or three

lines.speaker: FLUTE
lines.text: lords and ladies more married. If our sport had gone forward, we had

lines.speaker: FLUTE
lines.text: all been made men.

lines.speaker: FLUTE
lines.text: O sweet bully Bottom! Thus hath he lost sixpence a day during his life;

lines.speaker: FLUTE
lines.text: he could not have ’scaped sixpence a day. An the Duke had not given him

lines.speaker: FLUTE
lines.text: sixpence a day for playing Pyramus, I’ll be hanged. He would have

lines.speaker: FLUTE
lines.text: deserved it: sixpence a day in Pyramus, or nothing.
Enter Bottom.

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: Where are these lads? Where are these hearts?

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: Bottom! O most courageous day! O most happy hour!

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: Masters, I am to discourse wonders: but ask me not what; for if I tell

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: you, I am not true Athenian. I will tell you everything, right as it

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: fell out.

lines.speaker: QUINCE
lines.text: Let us hear, sweet Bottom.

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: Not a word of me. All that I will tell you is, that the Duke hath

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: dined. Get your apparel together, good strings to your beards, new

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: ribbons to your pumps; meet presently at the palace; every man look

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: o’er his part. For the short and the long is, our play is preferred. In

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: any case, let Thisbe have clean linen; and let not him that plays the

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: lion pare his nails, for they shall hang out for the lion’s claws. And

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: most dear actors, eat no onions nor garlick, for we are to utter sweet

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: breath; and I do not doubt but to hear them say it is a sweet comedy.

lines.speaker: BOTTOM
lines.text: No more words. Away! Go, away!
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: Athens. An Apartment in the Palace of Theseus

lines.text: Enter Theseus, Hippolyta, Philostrate, Lords and Attendants.

lines.speaker: HIPPOLYTA
lines.text: ’Tis strange, my Theseus, that these lovers speak of.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: More strange than true. I never may believe

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: These antique fables, nor these fairy toys.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Lovers and madmen have such seething brains,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Such shaping fantasies, that apprehend

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: More than cool reason ever comprehends.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: The lunatic, the lover, and the poet

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Are of imagination all compact:

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: One sees more devils than vast hell can hold;

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: That is the madman: the lover, all as frantic,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Sees Helen’s beauty in a brow of Egypt:

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: The poet’s eye, in a fine frenzy rolling,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Doth glance from heaven to earth, from earth to heaven;

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: And as imagination bodies forth

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: The forms of things unknown, the poet’s pen

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Turns them to shapes, and gives to airy nothing

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: A local habitation and a name.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Such tricks hath strong imagination,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: That if it would but apprehend some joy,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: It comprehends some bringer of that joy.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Or in the night, imagining some fear,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: How easy is a bush supposed a bear?

lines.speaker: HIPPOLYTA
lines.text: But all the story of the night told over,

lines.speaker: HIPPOLYTA
lines.text: And all their minds transfigur’d so together,

lines.speaker: HIPPOLYTA
lines.text: More witnesseth than fancy’s images,

lines.speaker: HIPPOLYTA
lines.text: And grows to something of great constancy;

lines.speaker: HIPPOLYTA
lines.text: But, howsoever, strange and admirable.
Enter lovers: Lysander, Demetrius, Hermia and Helena.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Here come the lovers, full of joy and mirth.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Joy, gentle friends, joy and fresh days of love

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Accompany your hearts!

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: More than to us

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Wait in your royal walks, your board, your bed!

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Come now; what masques, what dances shall we have,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: To wear away this long age of three hours

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Between our after-supper and bed-time?

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Where is our usual manager of mirth?

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: What revels are in hand? Is there no play

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: To ease the anguish of a torturing hour?

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Call Philostrate.

lines.speaker: PHILOSTRATE
lines.text: Here, mighty Theseus.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Say, what abridgment have you for this evening?

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: What masque? What music? How shall we beguile

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: The lazy time, if not with some delight?

lines.speaker: PHILOSTRATE
lines.text: There is a brief how many sports are ripe.

lines.speaker: PHILOSTRATE
lines.text: Make choice of which your Highness will see first.
[_Giving a paper._]
[_Reads_]

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: ‘The battle with the Centaurs, to be sung

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: By an Athenian eunuch to the harp.’

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: We’ll none of that. That have I told my love

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: In glory of my kinsman Hercules.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: ‘The riot of the tipsy Bacchanals,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Tearing the Thracian singer in their rage?’

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: That is an old device, and it was play’d

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: When I from Thebes came last a conqueror.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: ‘The thrice three Muses mourning for the death

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Of learning, late deceas’d in beggary.’

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: That is some satire, keen and critical,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Not sorting with a nuptial ceremony.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: ‘A tedious brief scene of young Pyramus

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: And his love Thisbe; very tragical mirth.’

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Merry and tragical? Tedious and brief?

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: That is hot ice and wondrous strange snow.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: How shall we find the concord of this discord?

lines.speaker: PHILOSTRATE
lines.text: A play there is, my lord, some ten words long,

lines.speaker: PHILOSTRATE
lines.text: Which is as brief as I have known a play;

lines.speaker: PHILOSTRATE
lines.text: But by ten words, my lord, it is too long,

lines.speaker: PHILOSTRATE
lines.text: Which makes it tedious. For in all the play

lines.speaker: PHILOSTRATE
lines.text: There is not one word apt, one player fitted.

lines.speaker: PHILOSTRATE
lines.text: And tragical, my noble lord, it is.

lines.speaker: PHILOSTRATE
lines.text: For Pyramus therein doth kill himself,

lines.speaker: PHILOSTRATE
lines.text: Which, when I saw rehears’d, I must confess,

lines.speaker: PHILOSTRATE
lines.text: Made mine eyes water; but more merry tears

lines.speaker: PHILOSTRATE
lines.text: The passion of loud laughter never shed.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: What are they that do play it?

lines.speaker: PHILOSTRATE
lines.text: Hard-handed men that work in Athens here,

lines.speaker: PHILOSTRATE
lines.text: Which never labour’d in their minds till now;

lines.speaker: PHILOSTRATE
lines.text: And now have toil’d their unbreath’d memories

lines.speaker: PHILOSTRATE
lines.text: With this same play against your nuptial.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: And we will hear it.

lines.speaker: PHILOSTRATE
lines.text: No, my noble lord,

lines.speaker: PHILOSTRATE
lines.text: It is not for you: I have heard it over,

lines.speaker: PHILOSTRATE
lines.text: And it is nothing, nothing in the world;

lines.speaker: PHILOSTRATE
lines.text: Unless you can find sport in their intents,

lines.speaker: PHILOSTRATE
lines.text: Extremely stretch’d and conn’d with cruel pain

lines.speaker: PHILOSTRATE
lines.text: To do you service.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: I will hear that play;

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: For never anything can be amiss

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: When simpleness and duty tender it.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Go, bring them in: and take your places, ladies.
[_Exit Philostrate._]

lines.speaker: HIPPOLYTA
lines.text: I love not to see wretchedness o’ercharged,

lines.speaker: HIPPOLYTA
lines.text: And duty in his service perishing.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Why, gentle sweet, you shall see no such thing.

lines.speaker: HIPPOLYTA
lines.text: He says they can do nothing in this kind.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: The kinder we, to give them thanks for nothing.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Our sport shall be to take what they mistake:

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: And what poor duty cannot do, noble respect

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Takes it in might, not merit.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Where I have come, great clerks have purposed

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: To greet me with premeditated welcomes;

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Where I have seen them shiver and look pale,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Make periods in the midst of sentences,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Throttle their practis’d accent in their fears,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: And, in conclusion, dumbly have broke off,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Not paying me a welcome. Trust me, sweet,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Out of this silence yet I pick’d a welcome;

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: And in the modesty of fearful duty

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: I read as much as from the rattling tongue

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Of saucy and audacious eloquence.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Love, therefore, and tongue-tied simplicity

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: In least speak most to my capacity.
Enter Philostrate.

lines.speaker: PHILOSTRATE
lines.text: So please your grace, the Prologue is address’d.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Let him approach.
Flourish of trumpets. Enter the Prologue.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: PROLOGUE

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: If we offend, it is with our good will.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: That you should think, we come not to offend,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: But with good will.  To show our simple skill,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: That is the true beginning of our end.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Consider then, we come but in despite.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: We do not come, as minding to content you,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Our true intent is.  All for your delight

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: We are not here.  That you should here repent you,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: The actors are at hand, and, by their show,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: You shall know all that you are like to know.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: This fellow doth not stand upon points.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: He hath rid his prologue like a rough colt; he knows not the stop. A

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: good moral, my lord: it is not enough to speak, but to speak true.

lines.speaker: HIPPOLYTA
lines.text: Indeed he hath played on this prologue like a child on a recorder; a

lines.speaker: HIPPOLYTA
lines.text: sound, but not in government.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: His speech was like a tangled chain; nothing impaired, but all

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: disordered. Who is next?
Enter Pyramus and Thisbe, Wall, Moonshine and Lion as in dumb show.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: PROLOGUE

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Gentles, perchance you wonder at this show;

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: But wonder on, till truth make all things plain.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: This man is Pyramus, if you would know;

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: This beauteous lady Thisbe is certain.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: This man, with lime and rough-cast, doth present

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Wall, that vile wall which did these lovers sunder;

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: And through Wall’s chink, poor souls, they are content

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: To whisper, at the which let no man wonder.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: This man, with lantern, dog, and bush of thorn,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Presenteth Moonshine, for, if you will know,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: By moonshine did these lovers think no scorn

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: To meet at Ninus’ tomb, there, there to woo.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: This grisly beast (which Lion hight by name)

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: The trusty Thisbe, coming first by night,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Did scare away, or rather did affright;

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: And as she fled, her mantle she did fall;

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Which Lion vile with bloody mouth did stain.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Anon comes Pyramus, sweet youth, and tall,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: And finds his trusty Thisbe’s mantle slain;

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Whereat with blade, with bloody blameful blade,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: He bravely broach’d his boiling bloody breast;

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: And Thisbe, tarrying in mulberry shade,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: His dagger drew, and died. For all the rest,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Let Lion, Moonshine, Wall, and lovers twain,

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: At large discourse while here they do remain.
[_Exeunt Prologue, Pyramus, Thisbe, Lion and Moonshine._]

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: I wonder if the lion be to speak.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: No wonder, my lord. One lion may, when many asses do.

lines.speaker: WALL
lines.text: In this same interlude it doth befall

lines.speaker: WALL
lines.text: That I, one Snout by name, present a wall:

lines.speaker: WALL
lines.text: And such a wall as I would have you think

lines.speaker: WALL
lines.text: That had in it a crannied hole or chink,

lines.speaker: WALL
lines.text: Through which the lovers, Pyramus and Thisbe,

lines.speaker: WALL
lines.text: Did whisper often very secretly.

lines.speaker: WALL
lines.text: This loam, this rough-cast, and this stone, doth show

lines.speaker: WALL
lines.text: That I am that same wall; the truth is so:

lines.speaker: WALL
lines.text: And this the cranny is, right and sinister,

lines.speaker: WALL
lines.text: Through which the fearful lovers are to whisper.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Would you desire lime and hair to speak better?

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: It is the wittiest partition that ever I heard discourse, my lord.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Pyramus draws near the wall; silence.
Enter Pyramus.

lines.speaker: PYRAMUS
lines.text: O grim-look’d night! O night with hue so black!

lines.speaker: PYRAMUS
lines.text: O night, which ever art when day is not!

lines.speaker: PYRAMUS
lines.text: O night, O night, alack, alack, alack,

lines.speaker: PYRAMUS
lines.text: I fear my Thisbe’s promise is forgot!

lines.speaker: PYRAMUS
lines.text: And thou, O wall, O sweet, O lovely wall,

lines.speaker: PYRAMUS
lines.text: That stand’st between her father’s ground and mine;

lines.speaker: PYRAMUS
lines.text: Thou wall, O wall, O sweet and lovely wall,

lines.speaker: PYRAMUS
lines.text: Show me thy chink, to blink through with mine eyne.
[_Wall holds up his fingers._]

lines.speaker: PYRAMUS
lines.text: Thanks, courteous wall: Jove shield thee well for this!

lines.speaker: PYRAMUS
lines.text: But what see I? No Thisbe do I see.

lines.speaker: PYRAMUS
lines.text: O wicked wall, through whom I see no bliss,

lines.speaker: PYRAMUS
lines.text: Curs’d be thy stones for thus deceiving me!

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: The wall, methinks, being sensible, should curse again.

lines.speaker: PYRAMUS
lines.text: No, in truth, sir, he should not. ‘Deceiving me’ is Thisbe’s cue: she

lines.speaker: PYRAMUS
lines.text: is to enter now, and I am to spy her through the wall. You shall see it

lines.speaker: PYRAMUS
lines.text: will fall pat as I told you. Yonder she comes.
Enter Thisbe.

lines.speaker: THISBE
lines.text: O wall, full often hast thou heard my moans,

lines.speaker: THISBE
lines.text: For parting my fair Pyramus and me.

lines.speaker: THISBE
lines.text: My cherry lips have often kiss’d thy stones,

lines.speaker: THISBE
lines.text: Thy stones with lime and hair knit up in thee.

lines.speaker: PYRAMUS
lines.text: I see a voice; now will I to the chink,

lines.speaker: PYRAMUS
lines.text: To spy an I can hear my Thisbe’s face.

lines.speaker: PYRAMUS
lines.text: Thisbe?

lines.speaker: THISBE
lines.text: My love thou art, my love I think.

lines.speaker: PYRAMUS
lines.text: Think what thou wilt, I am thy lover’s grace;

lines.speaker: PYRAMUS
lines.text: And like Limander am I trusty still.

lines.speaker: THISBE
lines.text: And I like Helen, till the fates me kill.

lines.speaker: PYRAMUS
lines.text: Not Shafalus to Procrus was so true.

lines.speaker: THISBE
lines.text: As Shafalus to Procrus, I to you.

lines.speaker: PYRAMUS
lines.text: O kiss me through the hole of this vile wall.

lines.speaker: THISBE
lines.text: I kiss the wall’s hole, not your lips at all.

lines.speaker: PYRAMUS
lines.text: Wilt thou at Ninny’s tomb meet me straightway?

lines.speaker: THISBE
lines.text: ’Tide life, ’tide death, I come without delay.

lines.speaker: WALL
lines.text: Thus have I, Wall, my part discharged so;

lines.speaker: WALL
lines.text: And, being done, thus Wall away doth go.
[_Exeunt Wall, Pyramus and Thisbe._]

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Now is the mural down between the two neighbours.

lines.text: No remedy, my lord, when walls are so wilful to hear without warning.

lines.speaker: HIPPOLYTA
lines.text: This is the silliest stuff that ever I heard.

lines.text: The best in this kind are but shadows; and the worst are no worse, if

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: imagination amend them.

lines.speaker: HIPPOLYTA
lines.text: It must be your imagination then, and not theirs.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: If we imagine no worse of them than they of themselves, they may pass

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: for excellent men. Here come two noble beasts in, a man and a lion.
Enter Lion and Moonshine.

lines.speaker: LION
lines.text: You, ladies, you, whose gentle hearts do fear

lines.speaker: LION
lines.text: The smallest monstrous mouse that creeps on floor,

lines.speaker: LION
lines.text: May now, perchance, both quake and tremble here,

lines.speaker: LION
lines.text: When lion rough in wildest rage doth roar.

lines.speaker: LION
lines.text: Then know that I, one Snug the joiner, am

lines.speaker: LION
lines.text: A lion fell, nor else no lion’s dam;

lines.speaker: LION
lines.text: For if I should as lion come in strife

lines.speaker: LION
lines.text: Into this place, ’twere pity on my life.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: A very gentle beast, and of a good conscience.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: The very best at a beast, my lord, that e’er I saw.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: This lion is a very fox for his valour.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: True; and a goose for his discretion.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Not so, my lord, for his valour cannot carry his discretion, and the

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: fox carries the goose.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: His discretion, I am sure, cannot carry his valour; for the goose

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: carries not the fox. It is well; leave it to his discretion, and let us

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: listen to the moon.

lines.speaker: MOONSHINE
lines.text: This lanthorn doth the hornèd moon present.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: He should have worn the horns on his head.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: He is no crescent, and his horns are invisible within the

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: circumference.

lines.speaker: MOONSHINE
lines.text: This lanthorn doth the hornèd moon present;

lines.speaker: MOONSHINE
lines.text: Myself the man i’ the moon do seem to be.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: This is the greatest error of all the rest; the man should be put into

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: the lantern. How is it else the man i’ the moon?

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: He dares not come there for the candle, for you see, it is already in

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: snuff.

lines.speaker: HIPPOLYTA
lines.text: I am aweary of this moon. Would he would change!

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: It appears by his small light of discretion that he is in the wane; but

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: yet, in courtesy, in all reason, we must stay the time.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: Proceed, Moon.

lines.speaker: MOON
lines.text: All that I have to say, is to tell you that the lantern is the moon; I

lines.speaker: MOON
lines.text: the man i’ the moon; this thorn-bush my thorn-bush; and this dog my

lines.speaker: MOON
lines.text: dog.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Why, all these should be in the lantern, for all these are in the moon.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: But silence; here comes Thisbe.
Enter Thisbe.

lines.speaker: THISBE
lines.text: This is old Ninny’s tomb. Where is my love?

lines.speaker: LION
lines.text: Oh!
[_The Lion roars, Thisbe runs off._]

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Well roared, Lion.

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Well run, Thisbe.

lines.speaker: HIPPOLYTA
lines.text: Well shone, Moon. Truly, the moon shines with a good grace.
[_The Lion tears Thisbe’s mantle, and exit._]

lines.speaker: THESEUS
lines.text: Well moused, Lion.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: And then came Pyramus.

lines.speaker: LYSANDER
lines.text: And so the lion vanished.
Enter Pyramus.

lines.text: Sweet Moon, I thank thee for thy sunny beams;

lines.speaker: PYRAMUS
lines.text: I thank thee, Moon, for shining now so bright;

lines.speaker: PYRAMUS
lines.text: For, by thy gracious golden, glittering gleams,

lines.speaker: PYRAMUS
lines.text: I trust to take of truest Thisbe sight.

lines.speaker: PYRAMUS
lines.text: But stay! O spite!

lines.speaker: PYRAMUS
lines.text: But mark, poor knight,

lines.speaker: PYRAMUS
lines.text: What dreadful dole is here!

lines.text: Eyes, do you see?

lines.speaker: PYRAMUS

lines.text: O dainty duck! O dear!

lines.text: Approach, ye Furies fell!

lines.text: Cut thread and thrum;

lines.text: This passion, and the death of a dear friend, would go near to make a

lines.text: man look sad.

lines.text: Beshrew my heart, but I pity the man.

lines.text: Since lion vile hath here deflower’d my dear?

lines.text: Which is—no, no—which was the fairest dame

lines.speaker: PYRAMUS
lines.text: That liv’d, that lov’d, that lik’d, that look’d with cheer.

lines.text: Come, tears, confound!

lines.text: Where heart doth hop:

[_Dies. Exit Moonshine._]

lines.text: No die, but an ace, for him; for he is but one.

lines.text: How chance Moonshine is gone before Thisbe comes back and finds her

lines.text: lover?

Enter Thisbe.

lines.text: Moonshine and Lion are left to bury the dead.

lines.text: In the church-way paths to glide.

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: And we fairies, that do run

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: By the triple Hecate’s team

lines.speaker: PUCK

lines.text: Following darkness like a dream,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Now are frolic; not a mouse

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Shall disturb this hallow’d house.

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: I am sent with broom before,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: To sweep the dust behind the door.
Enter Oberon and Titania with their Train.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Through the house give glimmering light,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: By the dead and drowsy fire.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Every elf and fairy sprite

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Hop as light as bird from brier,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: And this ditty after me,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Sing and dance it trippingly.

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: First rehearse your song by rote,

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: To each word a warbling note;

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: Hand in hand, with fairy grace,

lines.speaker: TITANIA
lines.text: Will we sing, and bless this place.
[_Song and Dance._]

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Now, until the break of day,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Through this house each fairy stray.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: To the best bride-bed will we,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Which by us shall blessèd be;

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: And the issue there create

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Ever shall be fortunate.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: So shall all the couples three

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Ever true in loving be;

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: And the blots of Nature’s hand

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Shall not in their issue stand:

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Never mole, hare-lip, nor scar,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Nor mark prodigious, such as are

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Despised in nativity,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Shall upon their children be.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: With this field-dew consecrate,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Every fairy take his gait,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: And each several chamber bless,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Through this palace, with sweet peace;

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: And the owner of it blest.

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Ever shall it in safety rest,

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Trip away. Make no stay;

lines.speaker: OBERON
lines.text: Meet me all by break of day.
[_Exeunt Oberon, Titania and Train._]

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: If we shadows have offended,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Think but this, and all is mended,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: That you have but slumber’d here

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: While these visions did appear.

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: And this weak and idle theme,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: No more yielding but a dream,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Gentles, do not reprehend.

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: If you pardon, we will mend.

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: And, as I am an honest Puck,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: If we have unearnèd luck

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Now to ’scape the serpent’s tongue,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: We will make amends ere long;

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Else the Puck a liar call.

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: So, good night unto you all.

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: Give me your hands, if we be friends,

lines.speaker: PUCK
lines.text: And Robin shall restore amends.
[_Exit._]
